sections.title: Tree and flowers
sections.text: Syzygium aqueum, the water apple, is a small evergreen tropical tree, typically 5–10 m tall with a 5–8 m spreading crown. Its opposite leaves are leathery; fluffy white flowers, about 2.5–3.5 cm wide, carry many long stamens.

sections.title: Fruit and food
sections.text: The glossy, waxy, pear-shaped fruit is about 5 cm long, with crisp, watery white flesh and sometimes a few small seeds. It is eaten fresh or preserved. Compared with S. malaccense, its fruit is smaller and usually paler; S. jambos bears rose-scented yellowish fruit.

sections.title: Plate
sections.text: The plate shows the opposite leaves, fluffy flowers and pale pink, bell-shaped fruit characteristic of cultivated water apples.
